items.rule: To pick the dealer, each player draws a card; the player with the highest point value is the dealer.
The dealer shuffles the deck and deals 7 cards to each player.
The remaining cards are placed facedown as the DRAW pile, and the top card is turned over to start the DISCARD pile.
If the starting card is a Wild or Wild Draw 4, return it to the deck and turn up another card.
If the starting card is a Draw 2, the first player must draw 2 cards (and forfeit the turn).
If the starting card is a Reverse, the dealer plays first and play goes to the right instead of left.
If the starting card is a Skip, the first player (left of the dealer) is skipped.
If the starting card is a Wild (not Draw 4), the player to the left of the dealer chooses the starting color and plays first.
The player to the left of the dealer plays first, and play initially passes to the left.
On your turn you must match the top discard card by color, number or word/symbol (e.g. on a Green 7, play any Green card or any 7), or play a Wild or Wild Draw 4.
If you have no matching card, you must draw one card from the DRAW pile; if it is playable you may play it, otherwise play passes to the next player.
You may choose not to play a playable card (reneging); you must then draw a card, and if it is playable you may play it, but you may not play a card from your hand after the draw.
Draw 2: the next player draws 2 cards and forfeits their turn; it may only be played on a matching color or another Draw 2.
Reverse: reverses the direction of play; it may only be played on a matching color or another Reverse.
Skip: the next player loses their turn; it may only be played on a matching color or another Skip.
Wild: the player names any color (including the current color) to continue play; it may be played even if you have another playable card.
Wild Draw 4: the player calls the next color and the next player draws 4 cards and forfeits their turn; it may only be played when you hold no card matching the color of the previously played card.
A player may challenge a Wild Draw 4 only if they are the one required to draw the 4 cards; the challenged player shows their hand to the challenger.
If a challenged Wild Draw 4 player is guilty, they draw the 4 cards; if not guilty, the challenger draws 4 plus 2 additional cards (6 total).
You may risk playing Wild Draw 4 even if you hold a matching number or word card of a different color (only color matters when it is illegal).
Before playing your next-to-last card you must say "UNO"; if another player catches you with one card before the next player begins their turn, you draw 4 cards.

A player cannot be caught until their second-to-last card touches the discard pile, nor after the next player begins a turn (drawing from the draw pile or playing a card from hand); if you catch yourself before being caught, you avoid the penalty.
If the draw pile runs out before anyone is out of cards, reshuffle the discard pile and continue play.
Two-player game: Reverse acts like Skip, and playing Skip or Reverse lets you immediately play another card.
Two-player game: after a Draw 2 or Wild Draw 4, the opponent draws the cards and play comes back to you.
A hand ends when a player plays their last card; points are tallied and a new hand begins.
If the last card played is a Draw 2 or Wild Draw 4, the next player must still draw 2 or 4 cards, and those cards count in the point total.
The player who goes out scores points for the cards left in opponents' hands, recorded on the score pad after each hand.
Number cards 0-9 are worth face value; Draw 2, Reverse and Skip are worth 20 points each.
Wild and Wild Draw 4 cards are worth 50 points each.
The first player to reach 500 points wins the game.
Alternative scoring: keep a running total of points each player is caught holding; when one player reaches 500, the player with the lowest points wins.
Partners (four players): sit across from your partner; when either partner goes out, the hand ends and the points from both opposing hands are scored for the winning team.

Partner variation with four players: play 12 hands (four hands with each other player as partner), each tracking points per partnership; the highest scorer wins. With eight players, two tables of four with 28 hands.

Challenge UNO: keep a running total of points caught holding; a player reaching the designated amount (500 suggested) is eliminated; when two players remain they play head to head with two-player rules, and the winner of the final hand wins.
